THE METHOD: declare strata and integer weights first, screen the population, REFUSE model-derived strata (selection must not leak which orders the model found hard, or the sample stops being blind), allocate by integer largest remainder, derive the seed from the population and spec digests, draw by keyed SHA-256. THE SEED IS DERIVED, NOT PASSED, because an operator-chosen seed permits seed-shopping - try seeds until the sample is convenient, publish the winner, and the draw still verifies; the docstring names what that does NOT close (label-shopping) and the pre-registration that would. KEYED HASH RATHER THAN random.shuffle because CPython's Random is not a specified cross-version, cross-language artefact and a draw nobody can recompute in five years is not auditable - which matters directly under a 15-year retention floor. FIVE REFUSALS, none satisfiable by taking fewer orders: below the fifty-order minimum, unstratified, eligible population smaller than target, a stratum allocated more than it holds, and a non-empty stratum allocated none. Spilling a shortfall into a neighbouring stratum would change the realised weighting away from the declared design with nobody deciding to. The spec digest is length-prefixed because a flat join is ambiguous across stratum keys of differing arity and two designs that digest identically derive the same seed. work_order permutes the selection under an INDEPENDENT key so the typist queue carries no stratum grouping, and the record stores selections sorted by id rather than grouped - it is read by people the blindness protocol keeps apart. Meenakshi found this while testing the correction paths. Selecting a field checks whether it is selectable; double-clicking to edit checks nothing.

I recommend refusing it: right now the two checks disagree, which reads as an oversight rather than a decision.
Should double-clicking a field you cannot select open it for editing?

tasks.title: A failed boot in production prints the DSN password to stderr
tasks.description: Vishwa proved it in core-api under a PRODUCTION config: a pydantic ValidationError attaches `input_value` - the RAW pre-validation dict, before any SecretStr exists - truncated to a head and a tail, so a short-enough secret sits in the window. A 5-char cookie_seal_password triggered an UNRELATED validator and published the app DSN password: input_value={'environment': 'producti...esql://u:PrOdPw123@h/d'}. Same in blind-svc. THREE THINGS MAKE IT BAD: (1) the validators are careful and it does not help - they interpolate only len(secret); the leak is in what pydantic itself appends. (2) The trigger is any of ~12 deployed-config refusals - wildcard allowed_hosts, empty CORS, docs enabled - i.e. exactly the failures a first deploy hits. (3) create_app calls from_environment() at app.py:48 and configure_logging at :50, so this is an UNCAUGHT TRACEBACK ON STDERR and the redaction pipeline does not exist yet - scrub_credentials matches that DSN perfectly and never gets the chance. OPERATIONAL: anything already deployed that failed to boot should be treated as rotate-now.
tasks.result: MERGED. Reproduced, fixed, RE-reproduced: the 5-char seal password under a first-deploy production config used to print input_value={'environment': 'producti...esql://u:PrOdPw123@h/d'}; now it raises SettingsValidationError naming cookie_seal_password and its reason, with PrOdPw123 absent from the entire formatted traceback. Same in blind-svc. TWO INDEPENDENT MECHANISMS, because either alone hides the other's failure: (1) hide_input_in_errors=True in model_config, covering direct cls(...) - the path every test uses and which never reaches the boundary; (2) redacted_settings_error() at the from_environment boundary raised `from None`, covering exc.errors(), which carries `input` whatever the config says. On the BaseServiceSettings hierarchy the flag is sealed by __pydantic_init_subclass__ rather than __init_subclass__, because model_config is not merged yet at that point and the check would read the parent's value and wave the subclass through. tasks.description:

A full `pnpm --filter @titlepipe/web test` reported 439 passed with two FAILs - FieldValueView.stories.tsx and StageDots.stories.tsx, both 'Failed to fetch dynamically imported module'.
